title: Attribute matching operators
learningObjectives: Explain attribute matching operators and write selectors that match the intended elements.

understand.concept: Attribute selectors match elements based on the presence or value of an attribute. Operators include exact equality (=), contains word (~=), starts with a prefix (|=), begins with (^=), ends with ($=), and contains a substring (*=).
understand.whyItMatters: Attribute selectors can target form controls and semantic attributes without adding extra classes. Use them for stable attribute meaning rather than fragile matching against incidental text.
understand.analogy: An attribute selector is like finding records by a field value or a defined text pattern.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; selector matching and specificity follow the CSS selector and cascade rules.

explain.narrative: The email field is matched by an exact type value, the reference field by a name prefix, and the autocomplete token by word matching.

examples.explanation: The email field is matched by an exact type value, the reference field by a name prefix, and the autocomplete token by word matching.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser applies the styles to elements that match the selectors.

practise.guidedTask: Create examples for exact, prefix, suffix, substring, and whitespace-separated token matching. Explain the difference between ^= and ~=.
practise.independentTask: Create a small document with several matching and non-matching elements. Write selectors for the required states and verify them in developer tools.
hints: Inspect which elements match each selector.
Keep selectors readable and tied to stable semantics.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Attribute matching operators</title></head><body>
<form><label>Email <input type='email' autocomplete='email'></label><label>Reference <input name='ref-code'></label></form><style>input[type='email']{border:2px solid #2a9d8f}input[name^='ref-']{background:#eef5fa}input[autocomplete~='email']{padding:.5rem}</style>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which operator matches an attribute value that begins with a given string?
questions.explanation: The ^= operator matches an attribute value that begins with the supplied string.

questions.prompt: What is a good way to verify a complex selector?
options: Inspect the matched elements and computed styles
Assume the selector matches every element
questions.answer: Inspect the matched elements and computed styles
questions.explanation: Inspecting the actual match set and computed styles confirms how the selector behaves.
